ARMED->DISARMED SAME-TURN, disarm owner 0.4.0_DS_ClientPlatform (me): the as-of resolver selected a NON-TRADING DAY. Measured 2026-08-24, the first Monday this producer met: the upstream netassets producer fires on a flat daily cron and had written 2026-08-22 (Sat) and 2026-08-23 (Sun) partitions re-stamping Friday's close; my filter tested 'p <= frontier' but never 'is this a trading day', so it selected Sunday and the run died NoSuchKey on bbg/2026-08-23/. It FAILED LOUD, which is the only reason this was cheap -- had bbg also written weekend partitions it would have published Friday's numbers stamped SUNDAY, silently, on a client-facing page. This is NEVER#1's own trap sprung on a producer already using the calendar: I took the FRONTIER from the calendar and then filtered the CANDIDATES without it. Using the right instrument for one half of a comparison is not using it. Fixed, and the selection extracted into a PURE testable function (select_as_of) with 4 regression assertions -- the defect needed a real Saturday in the bucket to appear, so exercising it was not enough.

OBSERVATION/INERT, surfaced not chased (surprise channel 3.0.0_SA_CVO~Z, cc issuer 2.0.0_SA_COO~Z): the served allocation object carries a FOURTH bucket, `hedge`, which ETFS-TO1-AC8's invariant does not name -- the invariant sums cash + fixed_income + equity only. It reads 0.0 on all 4 books today, so the three-term invariant holds and this changes nothing about the PASS above. IT IS A LATENT TRAP RATHER THAN A DEFECT: the first book to carry a non-zero hedge weight makes a CORRECT build fail this criterion, because the left-hand side would then be missing a real bucket while sum(ALL holding weights) still counts it. Whether hedge is reachable from today's inputs is the issuer's question, not this seat's, and the criterion is the issuer's artifact to amend if so. Not edited, not worked around, and the row above is filed against the criterion AS WRITTEN.
